column1: # Open gaps (tools/bench.sh): a shortfall that is known and not yet closed. One line per gap, tabs between:
# linux: the metric misses its target against Linux's locked number (bench/reference.tsv); the bound is the
# ratio to that number it may not exceed. ratchet: it is worse than its own best (bench/ratchet.tsv); the bound
# is the value it may not pass, on the host named ("-": any host, a count). While a metric is no worse than its
# bound a run reports it OPEN and passes; past it, ERROR. A line is added by a commit that says why, tightened
# or removed by `bench.sh --update-ratchet`, and never loosened. No milestone is declared over a line of a
# metric it requires. Each line is work owed: close it in Silica, or decide the cost and move its ratchet with
# The bounds below are from the sessions of 2026-11-22 (the single-processor and device values from a session
# that had a stray process on one measured core, which those paths do not use: tighten them from the first

column5: at 84 ns against a target of 82.5 (Linux getppid 97 ns less 15%): 138.6 instructions on the path then; 113.4 since 2026-11-23 (the call no longer returns to its stub before scheduling, so no registers are saved for a caller), not yet timed. Waits for: bench.sh --only null when the desktop is idle, then what instructions remain that no guarantee needs

tied with Linux unconfined at depth 1 (15.4 us): the extra hop, device interrupt to driver thread to client, ARCHITECTURE.md section 7. Waits for: a completion path with one wake-up between the device's interrupt and the client, the driver still the only reader of its device's queues
the tail of the same extra hop unconfined: 22.7 to 24.1 us against Linux 17.4. Waits for: the same completion path as blk_read4k_qd1

tied with Linux unconfined at depth 32 (287,000 against 291,500 a second): the host bounds both. Waits for: fewer interrupts and doorbells per request at depth (completions batched per wake-up, submissions per doorbell) in the virtio-blk driver and the block queue
ahead of Linux (9.5 us against 10.25) but short of 15% ahead (8.7 us). Waits for: the same one-wake-up completion path as the block reads, in virtio-net and the network queue

boot went from 13.8 to 20.5 ms since the ratchet was set at the M2 exit; the cause is not attributed and no commit weighed the cost. Waits for: the cause found among the kernel and init commits since the M2 exit that touch boot, then won back or its cost written beside the ratchet

the tail went from 6.2 to 9.2 us since the ratchet was set; the cause is not attributed. Waits for: the cause found among the kernel's timer and scheduler commits since the ratchet was set (0e38e20 changed how an idle processor decides how it woke), then won back
